headline: North-West SLA breakdown, driven by a warehouse outage, is fueling the complaint spike.
body: North-West alone added 36 extra complaints, more than fully accounting for the rise; other regions actually improved [E1]. The root cause is a conveyor failure and picker shortfall at WH-07 on June 25, which cut sortation throughput and pushed deliveries past promised windows [E6]. Enterprise and SMB customers cite these late deliveries directly, with two accounts flagging churn or renewal risk [E2]. Operations independently confirms the backlog-to-complaint link, corroborating the SLA breach as the driver rather than a coincidental pattern [E4].

actions.action: Notify affected North-West customers and issue goodwill credits now
actions.expected_impact: Reduce complaint escalation and churn risk while backlog clears
actions.monitoring: Track North-West complaint rate and WH-07 throughput weekly

what_could_change: If WH-07 throughput recovers and North-West complaints don't fall accordingly, look for a second cause.
caveats: Impact figures are in complaint counts, not rupees, and no rupee estimate was computed.
